answer: Tie identity to a physical ocean sensor with a factory-burned key. The agent anchors a buoy with a hollow juniper-wood float, and it streams signed temperature and salinity readings every five minutes for two weeks. The ledger checks the stream against nearby weather stations and tide gauges, so a fake must mimic real local sea conditions across four thousand readings. Each buoy costs sixty to ninety dollars, and one device backs one identity, so a thousand fakes means a thousand buoys in the water. Trust is earned by enduring real conditions, not claiming them.
